title: The 15-Point Workflow Audit Checklist for Service Businesses
subtitle: Find the broken processes bleeding time and money from your $1M-$20M service business in 90 minutes

sections.title: Client Intake & Onboarding
sections.description: This is where most service businesses start losing time before they even deliver anything. Every manual step here multiplies across every new client.

items.text: Centralize new client information capture in one system of record
items.tip: Audit every place client data lives today (email, forms, Slack, spreadsheets) and pick one as the source of truth before automating anything

items.text: Template and auto-assign all client onboarding tasks
items.tip: Map your last 5 client onboardings and look for the 80% of tasks that repeat every single time

items.text: Automate welcome emails and kickoff materials based on workflow triggers
items.tip: Tie sends to CRM stage changes, not calendar reminders or manual buttons

items.text: Provision client access to portals, folders, and tools without IT tickets
items.tip: Use role-based access templates so new clients get the right permissions in under 5 minutes

sections.title: Project & Job Management
sections.description: If your team is copy-pasting job details between systems or chasing status updates, you're paying for coordination instead of execution.

items.text: Trigger tasks across all relevant systems when a new job is created
items.tip: One job creation event should fan out to project management, billing, and team calendars simultaneously

items.text: Consolidate status updates into one visible dashboard
items.tip: If anyone has to ask 'where are we on this?', your system has failed

items.text: Log and surface every team handoff in writing
items.tip: Verbal handoffs are invisible work; add a required handoff comment or status change to make them traceable

items.text: Build reusable project templates for every repeatable service
items.tip: If you deliver the same engagement type more than 3 times a year, it deserves a template

sections.title: Communication & Notifications
sections.description: Most communication problems are actually workflow problems. If people need to ask for updates, the system isn't doing its job.

items.text: Send automated client updates at every key project milestone
items.tip: Define 4-6 milestone triggers per service line and wire them to a templated message

items.text: Trigger internal team notifications from workflow events, not manual pings
items.tip: Replace Slack DMs with event-based alerts tied to status changes and SLA breaches

items.text: Maintain a single source of truth for all client communication history
items.tip: Pipe email, chat, and call notes into your CRM so anyone on the team has full context in 30 seconds

items.text: Auto-route escalations when deadlines slip or tasks stall
items.tip: Set SLA timers on every critical task and define escalation paths before you need them

sections.title: Billing & Invoicing
sections.description: I've seen companies leave 10-15% of revenue on the table because invoicing is manual and inconsistent. This section finds that leak.

items.text: Generate invoices automatically from completed project milestones
items.tip: Tie invoice triggers to deliverable acceptance, not a monthly manual review

items.text: Reconcile payments and flag overdue invoices without spreadsheets
items.tip: Connect your payment processor to your accounting system so collections work itself

items.text: Track time and expenses at the point of work, not end of week
items.tip: Real-time capture recovers 8-12% of billable hours that get forgotten by Friday

completion_cta.headline: You've Found the Leaks. Now Plug Them.
completion_cta.description: If you flagged 5+ items as broken, you're likely losing 20+ hours per week and 10-15% of revenue to manual workflows. Book a free 30-minute audit call and I'll show you exactly which 2-3 workflows to automate first for the biggest ROI.
